clue.text: Religious person, male, one of two higher in rank

parts.note: of two things, one is this and the other is the other
a superior is someone higher in rank

explanation.surface: A clergyman described as one of a pair who outranks the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of two' gives OTHER, as in 'one or the other'.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns is a religious figure by vocation and title.

clue.text: Movie star, with stitch in side, keeled over

indicators.note: keeled over says the whole assembly is turned over, read backwards in a down light
in says the word for stitch goes inside the word for side

parts.note: a side is a sports team
to stitch is to sew

explanation.surface: A film star collapses with a painful stitch in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' is a sports team, not a flank; 'keeled over' reverses the assembled TSEWEAM, reading upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1930s Hollywood actress was famous for innuendo-laden one-liners.

clue.text: Who I meant when confused about Italian's novel

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation
confused signals that the letters of those four words are mixed up

parts.note: IT is a short form of Italian, as in gin and it (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: Someone explains which person they had in mind while muddled about an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes THEWOMANINWHE, and 'about' wraps that round IT just before its final E. The 's is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkie Collins wrote this 1859 mystery story, an early sensation fiction.

clue.text: Mythological god raised in Tarsus or Ephesus

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the god's letters sit inside the two city names that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pagan deity worshipped in two ancient cities of Asia Minor visited by St Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'in' no job; it is the hiding signal. In a down light 'raised' reads the hidden SORE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Understand about daughter making one grow furious

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see'
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Realising something about one's daughter makes a parent livid.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming suddenly very angry.

clue.text: Area with lines laid in dock, 50 side by side

indicators.note: laid in says the area and lines are placed inside the word for dock

parts.note: to dock is to cut short or trim, as is to pare
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A harbour scene: fifty ropes laid out side by side in a dock area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' is the verb, to cut, not the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that run alongside each other without meeting are parallel.

clue.text: Mug newly married man outside in vestry

indicators.note: outside says the two words sit around the little word that follows

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them
a groom or bridegroom is a man just married

explanation.surface: A bridegroom is mugged outside, then in the church vestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is itself the letters that the robbery and the groom sit outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the room in a church where the clergy put on their vestments.

clue.text: Merry individual in charge of team of rowers?

definitions.meaning: merry is British slang for slightly drunk, having had one drink too many

definitions.text: individual in charge of team of rowers?
definitions.meaning: the cox of an eight-oar boat is a single person directing the eight rowers

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the phrase taken literally: a racing eight's cox commands the eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means tipsy, having drunk a little more than is wise.

clue.text: Island, source of cough syrup in original form

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter
in original form suggests the word is restored to some earlier arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: An island said to be where cough mixture first came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in original form' rearranges SYRUP into YPRUS.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mediterranean nation lies south of Turkey on its own island.

clue.text: Look angry pointing to blot on the landscape

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
sore means angry or aggrieved, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: Someone glares furiously at an ugly building spoiling the view.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe an ugly sight, such as a building that spoils the view.

clue.text: Like tyres found in the undergrowth, son and husband ditched?

indicators.note: ditched says the two family members are thrown out of the word for undergrowth

parts.note: a shrubbery is a mass of bushes, a kind of undergrowth
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Tyres dumped in the bushes, with a son and husband abandoned there too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditched' takes S and H from the front of SHRUBBERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyres are made of rubber, so they have a bouncy, elastic texture.

clue.text: College register returned

indicators.note: returned says the word for register is read backwards

parts.note: to register something is to note it

explanation.surface: A college's enrolment list being sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous public school near Windsor is formally named a college, Eton College.

clue.text: Justifiably popular, always? Goodness gracious me

parts.note: 'well' can mean with good reason, as in 'you may well ask'
in means fashionable or popular
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something has deserved lasting popularity, then exclaims in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of astonishment, interchangeable in a startled reply.

clue.text: Partner improved on fifty per cent

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
fifty per cent is a half

explanation.surface: A partner has done better than an even share.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular term for one's spouse.

clue.text: Tricky question brought to light in quite a sermon

indicators.note: brought to light in says the letters are revealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A puzzling question raised during a long church sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or problem that is hard to solve.

clue.text: Carry weapons to support members

parts.note: to bear a load is to support it
arms are limbs, and members is an old word for limbs

explanation.surface: Bearing weapons in order to back up the members of some group.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from the US Second Amendment means to possess or be armed with guns.

clue.text: Strong wind that's got up breaks safety device in body of plane

indicators.note: breaks says the reversed wind goes into the middle of the safety device

parts.note: a fuse is an electrical safety device

indicators.note: got up says the wind's letters are read upwards, backwards in a down light

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A rising gale snaps a safety device inside an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's got up' reverses the wind to ELAG, reading upwards in this down light; 'breaks' splits the safety device around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main hull of an aircraft holding crew and passengers.

clue.text: Indicate fielding position elsewhere

parts.note: point is a cricket fielding position square of the batsman on the off side
out means away or not here, as in 'she's out'

explanation.surface: Showing a cricketer where to stand in another part of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point is a fielder placed level with the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to show or draw attention to it.

clue.text: Friendly foreign correspondent, perhaps

parts.note: not a journalist abroad but someone overseas you write letters to as a friend

explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign correspondent' suggests a news reporter; here it is just someone abroad who writes to you.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend made through exchanging letters, often living in another country.

clue.text: Attempt mostly opaque sort of novel like 'Frankenstein'?

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: mostly says the word for opaque loses its last letter

parts.note: something thick, like fog, cannot be seen through

explanation.surface: Trying to make sense of a murky horror story like Mary Shelley's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the K from THICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's book belongs to the Gothic genre of horror and mystery fiction.

clue.text: Greek cast in series causes annoyance

indicators.note: cast in says the abbreviation is thrown inside the word for series

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things or events

explanation.surface: A Greek actor in a TV series is a source of irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' hints at actors in a show but here means thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or irritation at having failed or been humiliated.

clue.text: Complain tearfully as name appears in jeans upside-down

indicators.note: upside-down says the whole is read from bottom to top in this down light
appears in says the abbreviation is placed inside the jeans

parts.note: Levis are a well-known brand of denim jeans

explanation.surface: Someone whines because a name tag shows up inverted in their jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: N inside LEVIS gives LEVINS, which 'upside-down' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to whimper and sniff while crying or complaining.

clue.text: Battle involving the British? Could it be Salerno?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the two words say 'new' (rearranged) ORLEANS, and rearranging those letters gives the Italian place Salerno

explanation.surface: Asking whether a British battle might have been at Salerno, scene of a 1943 landing.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer's first word acts as an anagram signal on its second, which makes SALERNO.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1815 battle in Louisiana saw American forces defeat a British army.

clue.text: Huge Greek character losing face

indicators.note: losing face says the front letter is removed from the Greek letter

parts.note: omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A huge Greek man suffering humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal for enormous or tremendous.

clue.text: Clerical dignitary heading off soon

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the cleric is removed

parts.note: a canon is a senior member of a cathedral's clergy

explanation.surface: A senior churchman is about to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like departing, but it removes the head letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word for shortly or presently.

clue.text: Bail out sailor, a pantomime hero

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of bail are put out of order

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A pantomime character is told to scoop water out of a boat alongside a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BAIL into ALIB. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show based on fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcutter from the Arabian Nights tale is a stock lead in British Christmas pantomimes.

clue.text: Condiment that may be given a shaking before starter in restaurant?

indicators.note: a shaking jumbles the letters of 'given' into a new order
the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dressing bottle shaken before the first course is served in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' rearranges GIVEN into VINEG; 'starter in' gives R, the first letter of restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is a sour liquid used as a seasoning or dressing for food.

clue.text: Whiskey taken by big-band leader after grouse dish

indicators.note: after says the whiskey and bandleader come later than the complaint

parts.note: to beef is slang for complain, as is to grouse
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Duke Ellington led a famous jazz big band

explanation.surface: A jazz bandleader drinks whisky after a shooting party bags game birds, before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb, to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic dish of fillet steak coated in pâté and baked in pastry.
